heard: A single storm on Saturn can wrap around the entire planet. Jupiter is thought to lack planet and circling storms, but Saturn periodically erupts with colossal great white spots. Six of these megastorms have emerged since 1876, returning roughly every 20 to 30 years. In late 2010, NASA's Cassini spacecraft watched a storm head grow to the size of Earth. The Tempest generated up to 10 lightning flashes per second while whipping out a massive tail. Within six months, that tail wrapped entirely around Saturn until it caught up with itself. Caltech scientists discovered heavy water vapor suppresses atmospheric convection for decades until cooling overrides it. Chemical remnants from these violent eruptions actually linger in Saturn's skies for centuries. Those deep atmospheric scars remain until Saturn unleashes its next planetary monster.
